title: Anesthesia POCUS — Cardiac, Airway, Lung, Vascular, Neuraxial
keywords: tracheal ring sign vs snow globe
sources: Critical Vector — Anesthesia Reference: POCUS (ASE 2022, SCA 2023, DAS 2015, ASA 2022, ASRA 2023)

changelog.change: Initial entry — cardiac 5-view sequence + hypotension differential + IVC table, airway US (CTM mark, ETT confirmation, gastric grading), lung US OR context, vascular access, neuraxial pre-scan.

summary: Five focused domains that change the anesthetic plan at the bedside: cardiac (induction agent choice, the intraoperative hypotension differential), gastric (aspiration risk before induction), airway (mark the cricothyroid membrane before a predicted difficult airway), lung (mainstem vs pneumothorax), and neuraxial (pre-scan the difficult back).

rows: 3rd–4th ICS left sternal border, marker → right shoulder
LVOT, mitral valve, aortic root, pericardium
Papillary level: D-sign (RV pressure/volume overload), RV size
EF, RV:LV ratio, valves, LVOT VTI
Probe flat, aim at left shoulder

items: LVEF by eyeball: good > 55% / moderate 30–55% / poor < 30% (EPSS > 8 mm suggests reduced EF) — guides induction agent and dose.
Regional wall motion abnormality: document pre-op; may change the plan.
Pericardial effusion with RV diastolic + RA systolic collapse + IVC plethora = tamponade physiology — a strong caution against neuraxial if haemodynamically significant.

rows: Hyperdynamic LV, walls kissing in systole, flat/collapsing IVC < 1.5 cm
Poor EF, dilated LV, plethoric IVC > 2.5 cm, B-lines
RV strain (D-sign, McConnell), effusion + RV collapse, or absent lung sliding

items: Cricothyroid membrane: linear probe transverse, midline; slide caudally from the thyroid cartilage — the CTM is a hyperechoic flat line between thyroid and cricoid. Skin-mark it before induction in any predicted or known difficult airway (critical for scalpel-bougie FONA).
ETT confirmation — tracheal ring sign: transverse at the suprasternal notch, a single ring = tracheal, two rings ('snow globe') = oesophageal. More sensitive than capnography in low-flow states.
Post-intubation: bilateral anterior lung sliding = bilateral ventilation; unilateral = mainstem → withdraw 1–2 cm.
Subcostal antral view, right lateral decubitus or supine, curvilinear probe.
Grade 0 — empty in both positions (antral CSA < 340 mm²) → standard induction.
Grade 1 — clear fluid in the right-lateral position only → consider a modified RSI.
Grade 2 — solid content, or clear fluid in both positions → RSI or awake technique.

rows: Decompress; find the lung point to localise
Chest tube vs needle per haemodynamics
Absent sliding on the operative side, present on the ventilated side — more reliable than auscultation in a noisy OR

items: Internal jugular: short-axis; IJ is lateral to the carotid and compressible; confirm the wire is in the vein before dilation.
Subclavian / axillary: infraclavicular, in-plane long-axis; axillary vein medial to the artery; real-time guidance reduces pneumothorax vs landmark.
Radial artery: long-axis improves first-pass success, especially in the vasoconstricted / hypotensive patient.
Femoral: CFV is medial to the CFA at the inguinal crease; stay above the femoral bifurcation.
Paramedian sagittal oblique (curvilinear, lateral to midline, cephalad tilt): identify the laminae ('saw-tooth') and the ligamentum flavum–dura complex; count levels from the sacrum cephalad.
Transverse interlaminar (midline, between spinous processes): measure skin-to-LFD-complex depth = expected Tuohy depth (typically 4–8 cm; varies widely).
Tuffier's line ≈ L4; ultrasound is markedly more accurate than palpation for level identification in the obese, scoliotic, or previously instrumented spine.
An OB epidural pre-scan reduces needle passes and complications — mark the optimal interspace before positioning, highest value at BMI > 35, scoliosis, or prior spinal instrumentation.
